docRequirement: memory.md:95-107 binds CLAUDE.md-family instruction files to `@path/to/import` expansion: "CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using `@path/to/import` syntax", and the imports are recognised "anywhere in your CLAUDE.md" — the page's own example block carries TWO imports mid-sentence on one line ("See @README for project overview and @package.json for available npm commands for this project.") and one after a list bullet ("- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md"), plus "- @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md" at :116. Recognition is by position only, with exactly two documented exclusions (:99): "Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks… writing `` `@README` `` keeps the text literal, while `@README` outside backticks imports the file." So a bare extensionless `@README` and a mid-line `@package.json` are both imports, and both relative and absolute paths are allowed (:97).
current:
Two separate parsers exist and both gate on the line START, and the file family the doc sentence is actually about gets no expansion at all.

(1) The live parser. `parseMemoryImportPath` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:49-64) computes `const trimmed = line.trim()` (:50) and returns null unless the trimmed line ITSELF begins with `@` — `if (!trimmed.startsWith('@') || trimmed.startsWith('@@')) return null;` (:55-57). There is no scan of the line interior and no code-span/fence state anywhere in the function. It also rejects a whole-line candidate that has no `/`, no `\`, no leading `.` and no `.md` suffix (:60-62), so `@README` and `@package.json` are not imports even on their own line. Executed against the shipped export under `bun test`: "See @README … and @package.json …" => null, "- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md" => null, "- @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md" => null, "@README" => null, "@package.json" => null; only "@AGENTS.md" => "AGENTS.md" and "  @docs/git-instructions.md" => "docs/git-instructions.md" resolve.

(2) Its consumers. `readMemoryFileWithImports` (memory-store.ts:66-110) walks line by line and REPLACES the whole line with the imported body (:82-107) — one import per line by construction. `memoryFileRecords` in the inventory pass uses the same parser (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:427-429). `base-agent.ts:1005` drops any line that parses as an import from the pinned memory block.

(3) Instruction files get NO expansion. `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md', 'CLAUDE.local.md']` (native-sources.ts:82) are emitted by `fileRecord('instruction', …)` (native-sources.ts:347-367, called at :988, :1081-1086, :1089) — a single record per file, never through `memoryFileRecords`' walker. Only MEMORY.md and rules files reach that walker (:691, :909, :978, :1027, :1092). The instruction record becomes a prompt layer at resolver.ts:966 (`case 'instruction': return { kind: 'instruction', layer: { key, resource, order } }` — no import metadata, unlike the memory case at :967-976), is routed at views.ts:215-216, and base-agent.ts:966-974 pushes `await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)` VERBATIM; the import-stripping filter at :1005 sits in the separate `runtime.view.memory` loop. `materializer.readText` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:169-184) returns the raw file bytes. `native-sources.ts:815-816` states "import materialization belongs to the eager inventory pass" — for instruction files that pass does nothing of the kind.

(4) The legacy route has the same line-start gate and is off by default. `parseContextImportLine` (packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:74-87) also does `trimmed.startsWith('@')`, and additionally rejects any path containing whitespace or an absolute path; `expandContextFileImports` (:89-134) also drops anything resolving outside the file's own directory (:109-111). It runs from `getProjectContextFilesPrompt` only when the capability runtime is inactive (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:256-257), and SessionManager installs a capability runtime on every turn (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5922, 7479, 9735, 11513, 12275), so this route is not the live one.

(5) One backend is exempt. packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305 passes `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']`, delegating CLAUDE.md loading to the Agent SDK, so Claude's own semantics apply there — but `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is off by default and the default Pi backend uses our parser.
divergence:
Three deltas, all in the recognition rule rather than in the values it produces.

A. POSITION. We require the `@path` token to be the first non-whitespace on the line (memory-store.ts:55-57 and, in the dead legacy route, prompts/system.ts:76-78); the page requires recognition anywhere in the line, with more than one token per line permitted. Every one of the page's three examples fails ours.

B. FILE FAMILY. The expansion exists for MEMORY.md and `.agents/rules`/`.claude/rules` only. For AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md — the files memory.md:95 is about — no import is expanded at all on the live path, whole-line or not, and the raw `@…` line reaches the model as literal text. This repo's own `CLAUDE.md` containing `@AGENTS.md` only appears to work because AGENTS.md is independently discovered as its own instruction record (native-sources.ts:988/:1089).

C. TOKEN SHAPE AND EXCLUSIONS. `@README` and `@package.json` are rejected by the extension/separator heuristic at memory-store.ts:60-62 although the page names `@README` explicitly as an import; and we implement neither documented exclusion as an exclusion — a backticked `` `@README` `` happens to be skipped only because the backtick displaces the `@` from position 0, and a whole-line `@path` inside a ``` fence IS imported, which the page forbids.

Not a value/key-name mismatch and not an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3's nine dated decisions do not touch memory import parsing. The one Nessy-specific behaviour here, the extra `@import <path>` form (memory-store.ts:51-53), ADDS a shape rather than removing one.

change.what: Replace the line-start gate with a line-interior scanner. Add `export function scanMemoryImportTokens(line: string, state: { inFence: boolean }): Array<{ start: number; end: number; path: string }>` that: toggles `state.inFence` on a ``` or ~~~ fence line and returns [] while inside one; skips regions inside backtick code spans; matches `@` tokens that are preceded by start-of-line or whitespace/punctuation (so an email-like `a@b` is not a token) and not `@@` (keep the existing escape, and unescape `@@` to a literal `@` in the emitted text); takes the path as the run up to whitespace, and strips one trailing sentence punctuation char (`.`/`,`/`)`/`:`) so `…@package.json for available…` yields `package.json`. DELETE the extension/separator heuristic at :60-62 — `@README` and `@package.json` must resolve — and instead drop a token only when the resolved target is not an existing file (the caller already does this at :90-98). Keep the whole-line `@import <path>` form at :51-53 unchanged. Keep `parseMemoryImportPath` as a thin whole-line wrapper only if a caller still needs it; otherwise remove it and migrate the three call sites. Then change `readMemoryFileWithImports` (:82-107) to substitute each token IN PLACE within the line (splice by span, right-to-left) instead of replacing the whole line, so a line with two imports inlines both and keeps its prose. Note `MEMORY_IMPORT_DEPTH_LIMIT = 5` (:11) against the page's "maximum depth of four hops" is a separate divergence; do not silently change it here.

Add a test rather than new code.

blastRadius:
Crosses a persistence/wire boundary in two places, which is a risk trigger in this repo.

(1) CAPABILITY GENERATION. Making instruction files emit imported child records changes the record set that `computeGeneration` hashes (capabilities/resolver.ts), which keys `base-agent.ts`'s `pinnedCapabilityContextCache` (:753-775) and every capability-catalog consumer. Every existing snapshot generation changes on first run after the fix.

(2) HOOK PAYLOAD. `eagerInstructionFiles` feeds the documented `InstructionsLoaded` event with `file_path` / `memory_type` / `parent_file_path` (base-agent.ts:968-973, :1009-1012). New imported entries appear there, and a hook consumer counting loaded instruction files sees more of them.

Other readers of the same layers: `runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)` at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4253, :4564, :4749, :10773 renders layer content into session/Sources UI surfaces — those show the file as stored, so after the fix the UI and the model see different text unless they are updated together. `parseMemoryImportPath` has exactly three call sites today (memory-store.ts:83, native-sources.ts:428, base-agent.ts:1005) and all three change signature or semantics. `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (memory-store.ts:317-334) and `loadUnscopedRuleMemories` (:289-302) inherit the new parser for MEMORY.md and rules. `runScheduledAutoMemoryCleanup` (memory/memory-cleanup.ts:260) rewrites the same files but does not parse imports, so it is unaffected. Imported-plugin paths are NOT affected: plugin bundles carry no CLAUDE.md family file. The Claude backend is unaffected by construction (claude-agent.ts:305 delegates to the SDK), so the two backends will still differ unless the fix is deliberately aligned. Containment: any widening of the walker's `relative(root, current)` guard (native-sources.ts:395-396) would let a committed CLAUDE.md pull a file from outside the project — that is exactly what memory.md's external-import approval dialog exists for, and we have no such dialog.
userImpact: Concrete and silent. A user who writes the documented form in a project `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` — "See @README for project overview and @package.json for available npm commands", or `- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md` — gets none of those files in context on the default Pi backend. The literal `@README` text is pinned into the prompt instead, so the model is told a file matters and never shown it, and there is no warning in the app, the Sources detail page, or the logs. The same holds for whole-line `@README` / `@package.json` (rejected by the extension heuristic) and for every whole-line `@path` in an instruction file, which the promptLayers route never expands at all. The failure is indistinguishable from the model ignoring instructions: the user's usual next move is to paste the content in by hand. In a MEMORY.md or a rules file, whole-line `@path/to.md` does work, which makes the behaviour look supported and hides the gap. Latent only on the Claude backend (off by default), where the Agent SDK loads CLAUDE.md with its own semantics.
